title: Core service and API
objective: Prepare the editor service for the MCP adapter and the library when those milestones start: an events long poll, typed host parameters, and per-photo selection with a paged catalog and relocation.
context_summary: The service has one write path, one planning path, one method table, one job table and API, declared envelopes and retry routes, errors that carry their facts as data and an explicit public surface; each fact is proved once. What remains is roadmap groundwork, blocked until its milestone starts and then done first. The owner's decisions and the programme's constraints are recorded in docs/decisions.md and docs/design/post-consolidation.md.

tasks.description: Give JSON clients an events.wait {after, timeout_ms} long poll that the owner parks and answers when the log passes after or the timeout expires.
extra_context: Wave 6, roadmap groundwork. Blocked: starts with the MCP adapter milestone on the roadmap.

Today an agent or another JSON client has no way to be woken by a change; it must poll `events.since` (`events_since`, `api/owner.rs`) on its own schedule. The desktop's own `OwnerHandle::watch_events` is a Rust-only wake callback, not something a JSON client can ask for.

The owner already parks a reply and answers it later for `OwnerMessage::AwaitSource`, so `events.wait` parks the same way: hold the reply until the log passes `after` or a timeout expires, then answer.
Events already name the asset and revision they changed, so a client can wait for a change to one asset as well as for any change at all.

acceptance_criteria: `events.wait {after, timeout_ms}` answers as soon as the log passes `after`, and answers with no new events at the timeout if none arrived.
Parked replies are bounded per client, so a client that never reads its answer cannot accumulate unbounded parked state.
The method is documented in the user guide and listed in `schema.list`.

steps: Test that a call parked before the log advances wakes on the next event past `after`.
Test that a call with no events before its deadline answers empty at the timeout.
expected_results: Both the wake and the timeout paths answer correctly, and no parked reply survives a client disconnect.

tasks.description: Type every host method parameter with the module parameter vocabulary, so schema.list gives each host method a schema an MCP tool can use.
extra_context: Wave 6, roadmap groundwork. Blocked: starts with the MCP adapter milestone.

`host_params!` (`api/params.rs`) publishes each host method's required field names, and for each optional field a free-text note such as "u64", "1..100" or "{mode:fit} or {mode:percent,value:10..1600}". A module's actions, queries, tasks and settings already publish typed `ParameterDescriptor`s (`modules/descriptor.rs`) through the same schema; the 69 host methods of the `METHODS` table (`api/methods.rs`) are the one place the parameter vocabulary is still prose.
An MCP adapter needs a JSON Schema per tool; without typed host parameters it would have to hand-write about seventy of them, the exact kind of second copy the method table exists to prevent.

Proposal: give each `host_params!` field a `ParameterKind`, identity kinds for asset, entry, draft, job, preset and artifact ids, integer and number ranges in place of the range prose, and one `json` kind for the handful of genuinely structured fields (`Zoom`, `AnalysisTarget`, `fields`, `settings`, `values`), so `schemas()` can list `parameters` for host methods the same way it already does for generated ones.

acceptance_criteria: Every host method's `schema.list` entry lists typed `parameters`, using the same `ParameterKind` vocabulary module descriptors use, with no new dependency.
The owner test that sends every listed field its declared value checks that each declared kind accepts a valid value and refuses an out-of-range one.
Structured fields that do not fit a scalar kind use the one `json` kind rather than a second vocabulary.

steps: Extend the owner's declared-fields test, `every_listed_method_accepts_its_declared_fields_and_refuses_an_unknown_one`, to check each kind's valid and out-of-range behaviour.
Compare `schema.list`'s host-method parameters before and after.
expected_results: Every host method lists typed parameters; the declared-fields test passes for both valid and out-of-range values.

tasks.description: Prepare the service for several photos: selection per photo, a paged catalog.list with summary rows, and a relocation change that moves the cached head.
extra_context: Wave 6, roadmap groundwork. Blocked: starts with the library or Locate milestone, or earlier if an agent client needs to work on two photos at once.

`PreviewSession::can_edit` (`preview.rs`) takes no asset and is true only while `selection == HistorySelection::Current`, so while a client previews a historical entry of asset A, its edits to a completely different asset B are refused as a conflict, and `render.sample`, `render.locate` and `preset.capture` on B without an explicit `entry_id` resolve A's selected entry instead.

`catalog.list`'s handler (`api/methods.rs`) takes `NoParams` and returns `service.assets()` outright; `EditorService::assets` (`editor/describe.rs`) runs one unbounded query and JSON-decodes every stored source interpretation on every call, on the owner thread.

`EntryCache` (`editor/entries.rs`) records history movement only (`EntryCache::moved` updates a cached head's revision, current entry and redo path); it has no way to record that an asset's own row changed. Locate, the first write that would change an asset's locator rather than its history, could not update the cached head, which would leave the cache's old locator in place until the catalog is reopened.

`source.inspect` already exists and already answers one asset's full interpretation, so the fix for `catalog.list` is to stop it returning that detail for every row, not to invent a new method for it.

acceptance_criteria: Session selection is keyed per asset, for example `selection: Option<(AssetId, HistorySelection)>`, and `can_edit` is checked against the asset a request names.

`catalog.list` accepts `limit` (bounded, for example to 500) and `after`, and returns summary rows (id, locator, kind, dimensions) with no source-interpretation decode; `source.inspect` remains the way to read one asset's full interpretation.
A relocation change moves the cached head where its write commits and emits an event naming the asset.
A two-asset owner test covers independent selection and editing, and a relocation test covers the cache staying coherent; the paging bound is documented in the architecture's limits.

steps: Two-asset owner test: selection and editing on one asset while previewing history on another.
Owner test: `catalog.list` pages correctly and decodes no source interpretation.
Owner test: a relocation moves the cached head and emits an event naming the asset.
expected_results: Independent per-asset selection and editing; a bounded, cheap `catalog.list`; a coherent cache after relocation.
